seo.title: 12 Design Subscription Services Worth Hiring in 2026 (Prices Checked)
seo.description: 12 design subscription studios with prices checked on their own sites, from $1,799 a month, plus how a design subscription compares with a brand sprint or a freelancer.

body:
A design subscription gives you a designer or a small team for a flat monthly fee, usually with unlimited requests handled one at a time and the option to pause or cancel.

Prices for independent studios range from about $1,800 to $6,000 a month, and product-focused studios charge more.

The big platforms like ManyPixels, Penji and Design Pickle are covered in my list of Designjoy alternatives, so this list focuses on smaller, senior-led studios and solo designers.

I checked every price below on each studio's own website on November 23, 2026.

Disclosure: I run Ebaq Design, which is one of the options, and I list it by price like the others, with its real drawback.

Design subscriptions compared

Sorted from lowest to highest starting price, with the studios that do not publish prices at the end.

1. Awesomic

Price: $1,799/mo for the Graphic Pack and $3,219/mo for the All-in-One plan, which adds web design and Webflow. A Dedicated Talent plan with its own project manager is priced on request. See the Awesomic pricing page.

Awesomic matches you with part-time designers from its network and lets you request a rematch at any time, at no extra cost.

Every plan has unlimited revisions, daily progress updates in its app and a flat monthly rate you can pause or cancel.

Work usually starts within 3 to 10 days, according to its pricing page.

Drawback: you work with whoever you are matched with, so quality depends on the match rather than one studio's taste.

Best for: startups that need banners, ads, decks and landing pages every week.

2. PAISANA.House

Price: €2,350/mo on the Standard plan and €3,890/mo on the next tier, both billed monthly, with a discount for paying annually. See the PAISANA.House page.

PAISANA.House calls itself a design membership: a dedicated senior creative working on one request at a time.

It lists unlimited design requests and revisions, with an average delivery of two to three days.

You pay month to month and can cancel whenever you want.

Drawback: one request at a time means a big branding project and a stream of small tasks compete for the same slot.

Best for: small brands that want a steady senior designer without a long contract.

3. eoo studio

Price: from $2,999/mo, listed on eoo studio's Contra service page.

eoo studio sells a monthly design subscription built for early-stage startups.

The plan covers branding and identity, product and MVP design, landing pages and marketing sites, and growth assets such as ads and pitch decks.

It promises unlimited requests, fixed monthly pricing, no long contracts and a satisfaction guarantee.

Drawback: it sells mainly through Contra, so there is less public detail about the team and process than on a full studio website.

Best for: seed-stage founders who want one team for brand, product and marketing design.

4. Ebaq Design (my studio)

Disclosure: this is my own studio. Price: a flat $3,000 per week for any design work, or $10,000 for a month booked upfront. See my pricing page.

It is not an unlimited request queue: each week has an agreed scope, and the Brand Sprint delivers a complete brand identity or rebrand in one week.

The Brand Sprint includes several logo concepts, a logo animation, colours, typography, brand guidelines, business cards and launch assets.

Bigger projects add weeks at the same rate, for motion, website design and development, and you work directly with me, with no account managers or junior designers.

Drawback: you pay upfront for the weeks you book, and there is no pause button in the middle of a week.

Best for: founders who need a finished brand fast, then design support week by week.

5. Designjoy

Price: $4,995/mo for the Monthly Club, discounted from $5,995. See the Designjoy website.

Designjoy launched in 2017 and is still run entirely by its founder, Brett, without extra designers or outsourcing.

You get one request at a time, unlimited brands and stock photos, and designs in about two business days on average.

You can pause or cancel at any time. For a full comparison, see my list of Designjoy alternatives.

Drawback: one designer and one request at a time make it slow for big branding projects.

Best for: a steady flow of web, app and marketing requests.

6. Designownow

Price: $4,995/mo for one request at a time, and you can add up to two more request slots at $2,995/mo each. See the Designownow website.

Designownow says it is an agency of one: you work directly with the founder, and partner designers help with animation and illustration.

Requests run through Trello, most are designed in Figma, and the average delivery is about 72 hours. Framer development is included.

Pausing banks the unused days of your 31-day billing cycle for later.

Drawback: each extra request slot costs almost $3,000 a month, more than a second designer at a bigger platform.

Best for: teams with fluctuating needs who want one senior designer and the option to pause.

7. Gr8r Studio

Price: monthly retainers from $5,500, projects from $8,000 and a UX audit for $1,500, credited toward a project. See the Gr8r Studio website.

Gr8r Studio positions itself as a digital product and AI engineering partner rather than a graphics service.

It offers a seven-day product redesign with Figma designs, a design system and a design.md file for developer handoff.

You can pause or end the monthly retainer on terms agreed upfront.

Drawback: it is built for product and engineering work, not logos and brand identities.

Best for: funded software teams that need design and build support every month.

8. Makeover Studio

Price: $6,000/mo on a retainer basis, plus $1,000/mo for an optional Stealth Mode that keeps your work off its website and social media. See the Makeover Studio website.

Makeover Studio specialises in redesigns, and its site shows before and after makeovers of apps, websites, brands and products.

You can submit unlimited requests, handled one at a time, with simple or related requests sometimes done together.

It promises delivery in about 24 hours for each request.

Drawback: it is built around improving what you already have, so it is less suited to a brand-new identity from scratch.

Best for: startups that have found product-market fit and need a fresh coat of paint quickly.

9. Kargul

Price: a trial week for $2,500, with projects starting at $10,000. See the Kargul website.

Kargul is a product design studio for web apps, mobile apps and websites.

You start with a one-week trial and move to a full project or monthly plan if it fits. Kargul says 95% of trial clients go on to hire it.

Its case studies include a trading education platform designed and built in eight weeks.

Drawback: projects start at $10,000, so it is a bigger commitment than a basic design subscription.

Best for: teams that want to test a studio for a week before committing to a product build.

10. Glyn

Price: Beacon from $3,000 for one deliverable, Launchpad from $10,000 and Anchor from $25,000, plus Lighthouse, an ongoing plan to keep the brand sharp as you scale. See the Glyn website.

Glyn focuses on brand design for cybersecurity and technology companies.

Launchpad takes about five weeks and is aimed at funded companies launching in the next 30 to 60 days, while Anchor is a three-to-four-month rebuild.

The bigger packages include three, six or twelve months of advisory after launch.

Drawback: its main offers are fixed projects, so the ongoing Lighthouse plan is priced on request.

Best for: security and B2B tech companies that need a credible brand before a raise or launch.

11. Baked Design Studio

Price: not listed publicly; you book a call through the Baked website.

Baked calls itself a design subscription for startups: a product design and creative brand studio for founder-led companies.

Its recent work includes brands and sites for Y Combinator startups such as OpenTag, Stoa and Context Dev.

The site lists case studies tied to funding rounds, from seed to Series A.

Drawback: there is no public price, so you need a call to compare it with the others.

Best for: venture-backed founders who want brand, site and product design from one studio.

12. Halaska

Price: not listed publicly; month to month. See the Halaska website.

Halaska embeds with funded AI, crypto and fintech teams to set the direction, design the product and ship it with the client's engineers.

It offers a senior designer on your product from the start, with brand, website and build under the same roof, directed by its founder, Chris.

It is based in Dubai and works with clients worldwide.

Drawback: it is a product design partner, so it is overkill if you only need marketing graphics.

Best for: funded tech teams that need a senior product designer without hiring one.

How much does a design subscription cost?

Budget subscriptions and marketplaces start around $500 to $2,000 a month, mostly for graphics and simple web pages.

Senior-led and solo-designer subscriptions, like Designjoy, Designownow and Makeover Studio, usually cost $4,995 to $6,000 a month for one request at a time.

Product design retainers, like Gr8r Studio and Kargul, start around $5,500 a month or $10,000 a project.

Compare what one request at a time really buys you: most studios work on one task at a time and deliver it in one to three days.

Design subscription, brand sprint or freelancer?

A design subscription is best for a steady stream of small tasks: ads, social posts, landing pages and product screens.

A brand sprint is best when you need one big thing finished, like a complete brand identity in one or two weeks. See my list of branding agencies that deliver in one week.

A senior freelancer is best for a focused project with one decision-maker. See my list of senior freelance brand designers.

Many teams combine them: a sprint for the brand first, then a subscription or retainer to keep design moving.

Can a design subscription do branding?

Yes, but slowly, because a brand identity is one big request in a queue built for small ones.

Most subscriptions will design a logo, but strategy, naming and a full guidelines system take several rounds that add up to weeks.

If the brand comes first, a fixed-scope sprint is usually faster, and a subscription can take over afterwards.

faq.question: What is a design subscription?
faq.answer: A design subscription is a flat monthly fee for ongoing design work. You submit requests to a queue, the designer works through them one or a few at a time, and you can usually pause or cancel the plan.

faq.question: How much does a design subscription cost?
faq.answer: Independent studios in this list charge from about $1,800 to $6,000 a month. Product design retainers start around $5,500 a month, and big platforms offer cheaper plans for simpler graphics.

faq.question: Is a design subscription worth it?
faq.answer: It is worth it when you have a steady flow of design tasks every week. If you only need one project, such as a new brand identity, a fixed-price sprint or a freelancer usually costs less.

faq.question: What does unlimited requests mean?
faq.answer: You can add as many requests as you like, but most studios work on one at a time. The real limit is how fast each request is delivered, usually one to three days.

faq.question: Can I pause a design subscription?
faq.answer: Most studios in this list let you pause or cancel at any time. Some, like Designownow, keep your unused days so you can use them later.
